### Compass Pathways Joins Forces with Leading Mental Health Organizations to Mark First-Ever U.S. Treatment-Resistant Depression (TRD) Awareness Day


October 14, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s204.q4cdn.com/927483861/files/doc_news/Compass-Pathways-Joins-Forces-with-Leading-Mental-Health-Organizations-to-Mark-First-Ever-U-S--Treatment-Resistant-Depression-TRD-Awa-ANY1F.pdf)


- First-ever Treatment-Resistant Depression (TRD) Awareness Day establishes dedicated moment to recognize and raise awareness of the condition’s profound impact on patients and their loved ones
- Survey data in a new report highlighting the significant burden of TRD on patients and caregivers to be released in a future communication


LONDON & JERSEY CITY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS), a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care, today announced the first-ever TRD Awareness Day in the U.S., a day dedicated to recognizing and advocating for individuals, caregivers and communities impacted by TRD. The campaign is being amplified by leading mental health organizations, including[National Alliance on Mental Illness](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nami.org%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=National+Alliance+on+Mental+Illness&index=1&md5=a69cf62d5470208c716b0485dd33ac2d) (NAMI),[Mental Health America](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmhanational.org%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=Mental+Health+America&index=2&md5=c090f40443de40f8cf75dee4bb15010a) (MHA) and the[Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.dbsalliance.org%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=Depression+and+Bipolar+Support+Alliance&index=3&md5=768bea2f07e47940d6ef9e19d38a1923) (DBSA).


TRD is a form of depression distinct from major depressive disorder (MDD) that is estimated to affect approximately 4 million people in the U.S., of whom fewer than 5% are currently on a TRD-indicated treatment.1,2,3 For many, the journey to recognizing TRD can involve years of cycling through antidepressant treatments that aren't providing meaningful relief, with an impact extending across work, school, relationships and daily life. TRD Awareness Day was established to increase understanding of this condition, help people recognize its signs earlier, and encourage conversations about finding the support they need.


“For too many people living with TRD, the daily challenges of the condition are compounded by feeling misunderstood, judged or even blamed when treatments don’t work,” commented Leah Wentworth, PhD, NAMI’s National Director of Science and Research. “TRD’s impact extends to their families and caregivers as they help their loved ones navigate the condition. As we recognize the first TRD Awareness Day, we have an important opportunity to bring greater visibility to this community, challenge the stigma and misunderstanding surrounding TRD, and remind those affected that they are not alone.”


A new survey found that of those living with TRD, nearly 95% describe themselves as either functioning but struggling, surviving day-to-day or barely getting by.4 Further, nearly two in three caregivers say TRD impacts the whole family's social, physical and/or mental health with more than half reporting that caregiving has taken a major toll on their own mental health.4 These results underscore how the burden of TRD extends beyond the individual and directly affects caregivers and loved ones, as well. The full report will be shared in a future communication.


“People living with treatment-resistant depression deserve to know that their experiences are recognized, their voices matter and there are people working alongside them to drive meaningful change,” said Steve Levine, M.D., Chief Patient Officer, Compass Pathways. “At Compass, we are deeply committed to the TRD community and to elevating the experiences of patients and caregivers as we work to address the significant unmet needs that remain. By bringing greater awareness to TRD, we can help build a future where people facing this condition feel understood, better supported and more hopeful about what may be possible.”


“When depression continues despite multiple treatment attempts, many people do not realize they may be experiencing TRD,” said Sagar V. **** Parikh, M.D., FRCPC, DBSA Scientific Advisory Board Vice Chair. “TRD Awareness Day can help both patients and clinicians better understand that this is a distinct condition, separate from major depressive disorder and recognize when it may be time to ask different questions about care strategies. Greater awareness is an important step towards helping people find the support they need and deserve.”


For additional information and resources about TRD, visit the[National Alliance on Mental Illness](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nami.org%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=National+Alliance+on+Mental+Illness&index=4&md5=099cff0c318cd583784a22e903cc28d3) (NAMI),[Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.dbsalliance.org%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=Depression+and+Bipolar+Support+Alliance&index=5&md5=3fbd5379ca8808cf7c481e1d616764e7) (DBSA) or[Mental Health America](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmhanational.org%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=Mental+Health+America&index=6&md5=1a9ee34ea3ac47e255c6937a123d6387) (MHA).


**About treatment-resistant depression (TRD)**


[Depression](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.who.int%2Fnews-room%2Ffact-sheets%2Fdetail%2Fdepression&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=Depression&index=7&md5=cc7537512f197074d03302ba07a4f8ba) , one of the most common mental health disorders, significantly impacts relationships, work performance, overall quality of life, and is associated with an increased risk of suicide.[Major depressive disorder](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Fbooks%2FNBK559078%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=Major+depressive+disorder&index=8&md5=c609f8716a61a3b6b60ae743658da92f) (MDD) has been ranked as the third cause of the burden of disease worldwide in 2008 by the World Health Organization (WHO), which has projected that this disease will rank first by 2030.


It is estimated that approximately 4 million patients in the U.S. with MDD live with TRD1.[TRD](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Farticles%2FPMC10503923%2F&esheet=54621570&newsitemid=20261014923063&lan=en-US&anchor=TRD&index=9&md5=76433384f6b1fc451ffe8efb214e2cc9) is broadly defined as an inadequate response to two or more appropriate courses of approved medications. TRD has a significantly greater impact on individuals compared to MDD, leading to residual symptoms, poorer quality of life, increased comorbidities, higher mortality, and an increased risk of suicide compared to non-treatment resistant MDD.


**About Compass Pathways**


We believe mental health patients deserve the possibility of a better future. Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS) is a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care. Our initial focus is developing COMP360 psilocybin, a proprietary, investigational, synthetic psilocybin treatment under evaluation for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). COMP360 is a potentially first-in-class treatment and has Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), as well as Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP) designation in the UK for TRD. We are leading the world’s largest classic psychedelic clinical program in TRD, and building upon that robust foundation, we are executing a late-stage trial evaluating COMP360 for PTSD, another condition with high unmet need. Our goal is to advance treatments that move the field of psychiatry towards treatment options that offer rapid onset and sustained durability with infrequent dosing.


Compass is headquartered in London, UK, with a U.S. office in New Jersey.


We are driven by our purpose of unlocking pathways to be – opening futures filled with possibility. Together, we are on an ambitious journey toward enabling people living with mental health conditions to find clarity through self-discovery, because every journey needs a Compass.
